retiredSubjects.note: Per-FILE retirement record for suites whose SUBJECT the A0/A1 cut removed. Round 72 (hosted-CI repair) deleted them, because a suite that cannot load (its module is gone) is not coverage — it is a red gate. Each entry states the subject it tested and why no preserved capability lost its arm. A file listed here is GONE from the tree; the entry stays so a reviewer can see the disposition without reading the deletion diff. The check reads `entries` only; this key is the record. A file that STILL EXISTS (a migrated or re-anchored suite, however it was edited) is NEVER a retired subject and must not be listed here — the live migrated population is declared in tests/checks/eb3-ute-migrated-suites.txt. Round 72 originally listed three live files here; the Round-72 deletion audit removed them and added the ten deleted suites that had no disposition at all.

retiredSurfaces.note: Per-SUBJECT retirement record for the A0 Family Contribution surface and the four instruments that graded it (scripts/eb3-family-definitions.mjs census + inventory arms, scripts/eb3-family-boundaries.mjs, scripts/eb3-tool-acceptance.mjs, scripts/ute-family-inventory.mjs). A0 retired the whole legacy execution plane (146 modules deleted, 2 entries replaced) in the frozen snapshot; the instruments that booked it were left grading a surface that no longer exists, which is 473 findings on the Required path and a red census. Each row here is one SUBJECT, its citation into the frozen inventory/decision, the exact frozen modules that make the retirement lawful, and the NAMED successors that carry the guarantee now: the frozen deletion list (scripts/ute-p0-assets.mjs --check), the dependency closure (scripts/ute-cut-closure.mjs --check) and the native execution-centre suites. A row is a LICENCE, not a silence: the check refuses a row whose citations are not tracked, whose frozen modules are not delete/replace in the snapshot, or whose declared surface is not wholly inside the frozen set and absent from the tree. A subject whose surface reappears is a resurrection finding, never a retirer. Read by scripts/ute-cut-closure.mjs (--check validates it), scripts/ute-family-inventory.mjs, scripts/eb3-family-definitions.mjs and scripts/eb3-tool-acceptance.mjs.
retiredSurfaces.frozenTreeNote: The commit that FROZE the A0 boundary (dev/agent-workflow/ledgers/ute-p0-assets.snapshot.json landed there, and the family plane still existed in its tree). It is the fixture tree the committed ute-family-inventory.json records and the source of the retired tool claim set — read by git object id, never copied.
